correctness.rationale: The assigned RESULT proof decomposes the (2q)-normalized Fourier matrix by a q-point DFT on both sampling grids. For residue r the remaining 2-by-2 block has off-diagonal Gram magnitude |cos(pi*d_r*theta)|, d_r=1 except d_b=m. Thus the complete 2q spectrum, rank defect exactly one at theta=k/m, and independence from b follow. The minimax is the maximum of |cos(pi theta)| and |cos(pi m theta)|. For odd m, both vanish only at theta=1/2; for even m, the barrier u*=sin(pi/[2(m+1)]) follows from the monotonic cosine on m*arcsin(u) for u<u* and the trivial u bound for u>u*. Taylor expansion at theta=k/m gives 2/(pi*m*|theta-theta0|). Independently constructed full complex Fourier matrices for q=2..7, m=2..11 and several offsets had spectrum error under 2.3e-14; this finite check does not replace the universal DFT/trigonometric proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural, fully quantified perturbation problem for periodic Fourier interpolation: one exceptional Fourier band, two regular interlaced sampling grids, and an optimally chosen offset. The exact all-dimension spectrum and optimal even/odd staggering law distinguish stability loss due to one altered character; resonant blow-up quantitatively matters for interpolation design. The two-by-two DFT method and scalar minimax are elementary, so the claim makes no stronger methodological novelty assertion.
